candidateAdjudications.reason: The finite verb 'contains' makes this an ordinary subject-verb sequence, not a noun cluster.

The lead-in "Because a settings file is a Python module, the following apply:" establishes the settings file as the subject of every bullet, so "It doesn't allow for Python syntax errors" has one referent. No competing candidate is grammatically available.
Second bullet in a parallel list sharing the same lead-in; "It" is the settings file, exactly as in the bullet above. The parallel structure removes any ambiguity the local word count suggests.

candidateAdjudications.quote: assign settings dynamically using normal Python syntax
candidateAdjudications.reason: This is a verb, object, adverb, and manner phrase; only 'normal Python syntax' is a noun phrase, and it is clear.

Third bullet of the same parallel list; the intervening code block makes the heuristic see "For example::" as the previous sentence, but a reader tracks the list structure and resolves "It" to the settings file. Referent is unambiguous.

"When you use Django, you have to tell it which settings you're using" — only Django can be told something, and it is the immediately preceding subject of the clause. The settings are the content of the telling, not the addressee.
